q: For a site that used to be a rice field, what soil condition should the foundation bear on?

scenario:
The national government plans to construct a government office building on land it owns within Metro Manila. The project has a Total Lot Area of 8,000 sqm, and the resulting structure will be a low-rise institutional facility built as a Basement + Podium (with parking optional) + Tower, on a site that slopes at 2%.

The parcel is a rectangular through-lot bordered on its north edge by an esplanade. That esplanade is nearly level, sloping only 1/3 of 1% and draining toward the east. The property's main axis runs along its 80-meter-wide frontage, which faces south. On the opposite side, the lot fronts a 30-meter-wide road right-of-way (RROW) that also drains east; the site itself slopes 2% down toward the esplanade. The esplanade frontage includes a 1.20-meter sidewalk, a 6-meter carriageway, and a 3-meter promenade.

Elevation 0.0m is set at the esplanade, and the flood line sits 0.50m below that datum. Along the 30-meter RROW, sidewalks measure 2.40m on each side, and a city ordinance has turned this street into an arcaded street. The design brief calls for green building practices throughout. Immediately east of the property stand two other government office complexes, while private low-rise office buildings occupy the lots across the street.

Design objectives for the project: (1) create a high-density institutional building; (2) design a facility that maximizes public service delivery; (3) give the building a landmark presence within its district.
